LESSON: SELF- EXPLORATION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Personal development
Topic 1.1: Self- Exploration

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Self- Exploration. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can personal abilities and interests influence career choices?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. appreciate personal awareness in day-to- day life

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SELF- EXPLORATION
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Self- Exploration helps you succeed in SOCIAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: SELF- EXPLORATION
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Appreciate personal awareness in day-to- day life

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate personal awareness in day-to- day life. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate personal awareness in day-to- day life.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Self- Exploration” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate personal awareness in day-to- day life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Self- Exploration is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “Self- Exploration” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: appreciate personal awareness in day-to- day life)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Self- Exploration to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: appreciate personal awareness in day-to- day life.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Self- Exploration from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Self- Exploration: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Self- Exploration?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can personal abilities and interests influence career choices?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Self- Exploration means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: appreciate personal awareness in day-to- day life.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
